title: Farkas Dual Rays Do Not Improve LLM-Based Optimization Model Repair

contributions.purpose: Test whether Farkas dual ray multipliers give better constraint ranking for truncated IIS feedback in LLM repair of infeasible optimization models.
contributions.mechanism: DualRayRank: extract the Farkas dual ray y from HiGHS (presolve disabled) for an infeasible LP, rank IIS constraints by |y_i| descending, and provide the top-K (with or without normalized weights) to the LLM for one-step repair.
contributions.evaluation: Presented as a training-free feedback interface with three conditions (IIS-TopK baseline, DualRay-TopK, DualRay+Weights) on MAMO-Optimization; for MIPs the IIS/dual ray computed on the LP relaxation.
contributions.source_quote: First, we propose DualRayRank, a method that uses Farkas dual ray multipliers to rank IIS constraints for LLM repair feedback.

contributions.purpose: Rigorously isolate the effect of constraint ranking from confounds and report the outcome.
contributions.mechanism: Controlled experiments holding model (Qwen2.5-7B), K=5, and greedy decoding fixed across the three feedback conditions, plus extended experiments varying K, samples, and model scale (32B, 72B).
contributions.evaluation: All three feedback methods produce identical results: 1/31 (3.23%) repair rate, repairing the same instance (EasyLP 425, IIS size=2); the truncation regime (16 instances, IIS>K) shows 0/16 repair for all methods.
contributions.source_quote: we report a negative result: dual-ray ranking does not improve repair under controlled conditions, and the truncation regime where ranking could theoretically help shows near-zero repair success.

contributions.purpose: Show that simple regeneration beats solver-feedback repair on this benchmark.
contributions.mechanism: Compare solver-feedback repair configurations against simple Best-of-2 inference scaling (2 samples, temperature 0.7, select first correct) on the same 7B model.
contributions.evaluation: Best-of-2 achieves 65.12% Pass@1, outperforming all repair methods including the best 72B configuration (58.86%, 34 samples) by 6.26 percentage points.
contributions.domain: Inference-time scaling vs repair for optimization modeling
contributions.source_quote: we demonstrate that simple inference scaling dominates solver-feedback repair on this benchmark, suggesting that regeneration is more effective than repair.

self_declared_provenance.quote: These approaches typically provide the Irreducible Infeasible Subsystem (IIS) as feedback, but must truncate large IIS sets to fit within context limits.

We hypothesize that Farkas dual ray multipliers can provide better constraint ranking for truncated IIS feedback ... Constraints with larger |y_i| are more 'responsible' for infeasibility and may be more useful for repair.
IIS-TopK (Baseline). Compute the IIS and sort constraints alphabetically by name ... This represents the standard approach in prior work (Ao et al., 2026a;b).
Farkas' lemma provides a certificate of infeasibility through dual rays (Andersen & ApS, 2015), and the IIS represents a minimal set of constraints that cannot be simultaneously satisfied.

notes: Explicit negative result (stated in title): DualRayRank does not beat the IIS-TopK baseline (both 1/31, same repaired instance; 0/16 in truncation regime), and simple Best-of-2 regeneration outperforms all repair methods including a 10x larger model. Extended gains are confounded with model capacity.
